query: Which material can be used for ductility, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Metals and alloys with a face-centered cubic (FCC) crystal structure exhibit higher ductility due to their ability to undergo dislocation-mediated plastic deformation.
generation.material_initial_state: Polycrystalline metals and alloys with varying grain sizes and microstructures
generation.intervention: Molecular Dynamics Simulation with parameters: simulation time = 10 ns, temperature = 300 K, and strain rate = 10^8 s^-1
generation.structural_mediator: Dislocation density and grain boundary structure
generation.mechanism: Dislocation-mediated plastic deformation and grain boundary sliding
generation.predicted_outcome: Increased ductility in metals and alloys with FCC crystal structure, characterized by higher strain-to-failure and lower yield strength
generation.baseline: Body-centered cubic (BCC) and hexagonal close-packed (HCP) crystal structures
generation.boundary: Limitations in simulation size and timescale, as well as uncertainties in modeling dislocation behavior
generation.uncertainty: The exact relationship between dislocation density, grain boundary structure, and ductility is not well understood and requires further investigation

falsification_experiment.design: Compare the ductility of metals and alloys with FCC, BCC, and HCP crystal structures using Molecular Dynamics Simulation and experimental tensile testing
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the simulated and experimental results show no significant difference in ductility between FCC and non-FCC crystal structures, the hypothesis is falsified
